title: What DNA Computing Arrays Is
definition: DNA Computing Arrays: computers running on DNA reactions.
description:
DNA Computing Arrays: computers running on DNA reactions. This is Future Computing Paradigms at its most ambitious — strand libraries research, array logistics engineering and reaction design operations converging on a single goal: making array hulls real.

Why it matters: Future Computing Paradigms will decide readout sequencing outcomes this century. DNA Computing Arrays is one of the load-bearing ideas: without working array hulls, the larger strand libraries vision stalls, and with it, the array logistics systems that depend on it.

This database documents DNA Computing Arrays in full: what it is, the real research behind it today, the pieces it is built from, dated forecasts, runnable demo programs, and a teaching ladder from foundations to mastery. Every record carries a working program you can run.

t: Real Research Today: DNA Computing Arrays
title: Real Research Today: DNA Computing Arrays
definition: Today's documented research behind DNA Computing Arrays.
description:
The road to DNA Computing Arrays is already being paved. Intel's Loihi and IBM's TrueNorth/ NorthPole chips advance neuromorphic computing. Reversible and adiabatic computing research (Sandia, Notre Dame) targets thermodynamic limits.

Lightmatter and Luminous Computing build photonic AI accelerators. Together these programs form the strand libraries foundation that DNA Computing Arrays will build on — the array logistics results, the reaction design methods, and the institutional memory.

Forecasts are projections, not promises: the dated milestones in this database reflect published roadmaps and expert surveys, and they will move as array logistics research advances. Treat every date as a planning scenario with error bars, and watch the signals listed in each milestone record.

description:
First array hulls cloud instances rent strand libraries logic by the hour to researchers worldwide.

Signals to watch: peer-reviewed strand libraries demonstrations, array logistics cost curves bending down, and operators — not vendors — reporting reaction design uptime. When all three flash green, 2030 stops being a forecast and starts being a schedule. (4 years from the 2026 baseline.)

title: DNA Computing Arrays Systems Simulator
definition: Simulates DNA Computing Arrays operating for a day.
description:
The simulator walks a DNA Computing Arrays installation through six operating steps, with seeded randomness standing in for real-world variation. Seed 96702 reproduces this exact run — change the seed in the program to explore other days.

Watch for DEGRADED steps: they mark where strand libraries monitoring, array logistics redundancy, or reaction design maintenance would intervene in a real deployment. A simulator that never degrades is lying; this one degrades about eight percent of the time, like early hardware does.

title: DNA Computing Arrays Master Roadmap
definition: The united roadmap for DNA Computing Arrays: prove, build, operate, compound.
description:
The master roadmap for DNA Computing Arrays — computers running on DNA reactions.

Phase 1 — Prove (strand libraries): laboratory demonstrations of every component, replicated independently. No scaling until the physics is boring.

Phase 2 — Build (array logistics): pilot manufacturing and integration. The six pieces meet for the first time and the interfaces get honest.

Phase 3 — Operate (reaction design): continuous real-world operation. Uptime, cost curves and failure data replace projections.

Phase 4 — Compound (readout sequencing): array hulls as everyday infrastructure. Costs collapse, standards settle, and biolabs-scale deployment begins.

Public edition: phases follow documented research readiness. This record unites the database: overview, research, components, milestones, demos and drills all point here.
